::: {#sol-autograd-slope}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
def mean_log_loss(theta):
    """Mean log loss of the soft 0-or-1 rule with cutoff `theta`."""
    p = torch.sigmoid(ink_01 - theta)
    return -torch.mean(is_one * torch.log(p) + (1 - is_one) * torch.log(1 - p))

theta = torch.tensor(5.0, dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
loss = mean_log_loss(theta)
(slope_by_autograd,) = torch.autograd.grad(loss, theta)
print(loss)
print(slope_by_autograd)
```

`torch.autograd.grad` returns `r sprintf("%.4f", py$slope_by_autograd$item())`.
The code for $\emprisk$ says nothing about its derivative.
Because `theta` was made with `requires_grad=True`,
PyTorch recorded each operation that turned it into `loss`
(the subtraction `ink_01 - theta`, the logistic function, and each operation after them, down to the mean and its change of sign),
and `torch.autograd.grad` applied the chain rule to those operations, one at a time.
The `grad_fn` that `loss` prints is the record of its last operation.

:::
